section.title: Wealth of Nations — taxation (BYOA test)
section.author: Adam Smith
section.summary: In this excerpt, Smith proposes four tests for taxation: contributions approximately proportional to revenue, certainty about the obligation, convenience of payment, and minimizing burdens beyond the revenue reaching the treasury. He describes how discretion, collection costs, discouraged industry, penalties and intrusive examinations can make a tax more burdensome.

ideas.name: Proportional contribution
ideas.explanation: Smith links contributions to the revenue people enjoy under the state's protection, while recognizing unequal effects across revenue types.
ideas.whenToUse: Examining how a tax distributes contributions.
steps: Assess contributions in proportion to the revenue enjoyed under the state's protection.
ideas.limits: The excerpt does not prescribe a graduated tax schedule or exact rates.

ideas.name: Certainty of taxation
ideas.explanation: Unclear obligations leave contributors exposed to collectors' discretion and possible extortion. Smith gives certainty strong priority over equality in this passage.
ideas.whenToUse: Reviewing whether contributors can understand a tax obligation.
steps: Make the amount, time and manner of payment clear to the contributor and others.
ideas.limits: This is Smith's stated principle; the excerpt does not quantify its effects in a modern tax system.

ideas.name: Convenient payment
ideas.explanation: Smith recommends collection when and how payment is most convenient, illustrating rent taxes paid when rent is received and luxury taxes paid as purchases occur.
ideas.whenToUse: Choosing the timing and manner of collection.
steps: Arrange the time and manner of collection to be most convenient for the contributor.
ideas.limits: The illustrations concern rent and luxury purchases; they do not establish that all consumption taxes are preferable.

ideas.name: Burdens beyond treasury revenue
ideas.explanation: Smith identifies collection overhead, discouraged industry, ruinous evasion penalties and intrusive examinations as ways taxation can impose burdens beyond treasury receipts.
ideas.whenToUse: Examining the burdens of a proposed tax beyond its nominal payment.
steps: Design the tax to take and keep as little as possible from people's pockets beyond what reaches the treasury.
ideas.limits: These categories are not a numerical formula and do not establish a preferred tax rate.

book.oneLiner: Smith evaluates taxation by proportional contribution, certainty, convenience and burdens beyond treasury revenue.
book.readIf: You want to examine a tax proposal using Smith's four maxims.
book.thesis: This limited excerpt treats tax design as more than the amount collected: how obligations are distributed, communicated and collected also affects their burden. It supplies four principles, not a complete contemporary tax policy.
